newsitem.title: USA: Rubin says Archer tax plan unfair to families.
newsitem.headline: Rubin says Archer tax plan unfair to families.

text.p: Tax provisions in a Republican proposal are unfair to working families and should be modified, Treasury Secretary Robert Robert Rubin said on Wednesday.

In a letter to House Ways and Means Committee Chairman Bill Archer, Rubin said President Clinton was "eager to sign legislation implementing the (budget) agreement into law but ... the proposal you have put forward does not meet the test of fairness to working families and has other serious problems."

Rubin said the Republican proposal reduces the value of an existing $500 child tax credit for millions of low-income families because they would be able to take it only after the earned income tax credit was taken against their income.

"A family with two children and $25,000 of income, for example, would receive no tax relief from the child credit under your proposal," Rubin said, whereas they would get a $1,000 credit under an alternative Democratic proposal.
Rubin said the Clinton administration favored a refundable child credit, aimed at low- and middle-income families, that was indexed for inflation.
In addition, taxpayers should be permitted to put their child credit in a tax-favored savings account to finance their children's education, he said.
Rubin said the current Republican tax proposal effectively "singles out six million families who pay for child care and gives them a smaller tax cut."
Beginning in 2002, it specifies that families who get a tax credit for their child care expenses would lose 50 cents for each dollar of their child credit, he said.
He said this and other measures in the Republican budget proposal thus favor the wealthy over the poor and working middle-class families and need revision to make them more equitable.
